memory_before.meridian-credits/release-1.0-agreement: Meridian Credits release 1.0 credit agreement (approved by Finance in issue trial-9f6, 2026-09-07). Scope: monthly statement quotes; a request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted statement; caps apply within that set. Rules: (1) Each line's uncapped credit is 10% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to integer cents. (2) A 2400-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same account_id, across its subscriptions; distinct account groups have independent caps. (3) Within a cap group, credit is assigned earliest service_on first; equal service dates use increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order). Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines get the remainder or zero. (4) Total credit is the sum of assigned line credits; a line's amount_due_cents is charge minus assigned credit; total due is total charges minus total credit. Line invariants: exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on (Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01..2099-12-31), charge_cents (nonnegative int, US cents); line_id unique within a request; subscription identified by (account_id, subscription_id); line collections may be empty. Release selection: omitted release selects the current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version; versions remain supported once introduced. Commands: single-line quote (implemented in trial-9f6; response keys exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents) and whole-statement total (implemented in trial-m30; request {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...]} with optional release; response keys exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; reuses assign_credits_1_0 in main.py so the per-account cap spans the full statement rather than quoting lines independently; empty statement returns all zeros). Sources: issue trial-9f6 description (Finance-approved agreement), issue trial-m30 description and implementation.

memory_after.meridian-credits/release-2.0-agreement: Meridian Credits release 2.0 credit agreement, the CURRENT agreement (Finance permanent adoption, applied in issue trial-tc8, 2026-09-07). Scope: monthly statement quotes; a request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted statement; caps apply within that set; applies to every supplied charge set regardless of service dates. Rules: (1) Each line's uncapped credit is 15% of charge_cents (charge_cents * 15 // 100), rounded down separately to integer cents. (2) A 3000-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same (account_id, subscription_id) pair; distinct pairs have independent caps (same subscription_id under different accounts is distinct; one account with several subscriptions is distinct per subscription). Note: for the quote/total commands the group total always equals min(sum of uncapped credits, 3000), so the priority order is not observable through them; it is implemented as specified for fidelity and any future per-line reporting. (4) Total credit is the sum of assigned line credits; a line's amount_due_cents is charge minus assigned credit; total due is total charges minus total credit. issue_completion.title: Apply the approved release 2 credit agreement
issue_completion.description:
Meridian Credits quotes loyalty credits for a subscription reseller. The local Python CLI accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON object on stdout; run `python3 main.py`. Preserve `{"command":"ping"}` -> `{"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"}` and the existing unknown-command response. No network, clock, locale or third-party package is needed. Malformed input is outside these issues.

A charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, and charge_cents. The three IDs are nonempty strings; line_id is unique within a request. A subscription is identified by the pair (account_id, subscription_id); the same subscription_id can occur under different accounts, and a subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31. charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by its service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order means Unicode code-point order. JSON object key order is immaterial; do not add response keys beyond those specified.

Release "1.0" is the initial agreement. An omitted release selects the current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version. Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward. Public suites name a specific release and send explicit release values, so their expectations remain applicable when the current agreement changes. Run a supplied suite with `python3 test_public.py --cases PATH`.


Finance has permanently adopted release 2.0 as the current agreement: Each line's uncapped credit is 15% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to integer cents. The 3000-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same (account_id, subscription_id) pair. Distinct groups have independent caps. Within each cap group, credit is assigned to lines in this priority: largest charge_cents first; equal charges use increasing line_id. Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group's remaining cap; later lines receive only the remaining credit, or zero. The total credit is the sum of assigned line credits. A line's amount due is its charge minus its assigned credit; the total due is total charges minus total credit.

Requests to quote and total with omitted release now use release "2.0". Support explicit release "2.0" with the same behavior. Explicit release "1.0" quote and total requests continue to use the original approved agreement. Request/response shapes are unchanged; the response release identifies the agreement actually used. This replaces the current agreement for every supplied charge set, regardless of service dates.

Example current quote request: {"command": "quote", "line": {"line_id": "L-1", "account_id": "A", "subscription_id": "S", "service_on": "2026-04-15", "charge_cents": 19999}}
Response: {"release": "2.0", "credit_cents": 2999, "amount_due_cents": 17000, "line_id": "L-1"}
issue_completion.close_reason: Implemented release 2.0 in main.py: assign_credits_2_0 (15% floor per line, 3000-cent cap per (account_id, subscription_id) group, largest charge then increasing line_id priority), quote_line_2_0, total_2_0; omitted release now selects "2.0" via CURRENT_RELEASE, explicit 1.0/2.0 both supported. Updated tests/test_quote.py and tests/test_total.py (omitted-release expectations moved to 2.0; 1.0 tests pinned explicitly; added 2.0 cap-group, rounding, and empty-set coverage). Verified: all 3 public suites pass (5 cases) and 20 unit tests pass. Knowledge preserved in memories meridian-credits/release-2.0-agreement (new current agreement) and meridian-credits/release-1.0-agreement (updated: original agreement, still supported for explicit 1.0).
